summary: Jan Dolensky specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He earned his Magister der Philosophie at the University of Vienna, attested in 2013, where he studied under MA supervisor Klaus-Dieter Mathes.

Jan E. M. Houben works in Indology, linguistics, and philosophy, having studied as a PhD student at the University of Lausanne (1990–1991). He has held posts at IIAS, Leiden University, and École Pratique des Hautes Études (Directeur d'Études, 2003).

Jan Filipský is a scholar in Indology and history/archaeology. He studied at Charles University (~1960–1966) and held positions at the Oriental Institute of the Czech Academy of Sciences (~1967) and the University of Chicago (~1996–1999, ~2010).

Jan Fontein specialized in history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies, earning his PhD at Leiden University under Theodoor Paul Galestin. He served as a curator at the Rijksmuseum and as curator of Asiatic art at the Museum of Fine Arts, Boston (1966–1992).

Jan Gonda was an Indologist and linguist who studied under Willem Caland (1923–1931). He spent his academic career at Utrecht University, serving as Chair of Sanskrit in 1929 and Professor of Indology from 1932 to 1976.

Jan Hanusz was a linguist and Indologist who earned his PhD at Leipzig (~1878–1882) and habilitated at the University of Vienna (1884–1885), where he also held a post (~1884–1887), studying under Karl Brugmann, August Leskien, and Georg Bühler.

Jan Jakob Maria de Groot was a Sinologist and scholar of religious studies who studied at Leiden University and under Georg von der Gabelentz. He held professorships at Leiden University (1891–1912) and Humboldt University of Berlin (~1912–1921).

Jan Jaworski was a scholar of Sinology, Buddhist studies, and Japanology. He studied at the University of Warsaw (~1921–1927) under Stanisław Schayer and also under Jean Przyluski, later serving as Privatdozent at Warsaw in 1930.

Jan Jetso Boeles was a scholar in history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Leiden University (1940–1945) under Nicolaas Johannes Krom and F. B. J. Kuiper, later serving as director of the Siam Society (~1968–1978).

Jan Julius Lodewijk Duyvendak was a Sinologist who studied at Leiden University, the Sorbonne, and Berlin under Édouard Chavannes and Henri Cordier. He served at Leiden University, becoming Professor of Chinese Language and Literature (1930–1954).
Jan Kornelis de Cock was an Indologist who completed his Ph.D. at the University of Amsterdam in 1899, where he studied under Christianus Cornelis Uhlenbeck between ~1893 and 1899.
Jan Kučera works in Indology, linguistics, and computational fields. He has held posts at the University of Reims Champagne-Ardenne (attested 2023) and Charles University (attested 2026).

Jan Laurens Andries Brandes specialized in Indology, history, archaeology, and linguistics. He earned his Ph.D. at Leiden University (1879–1884) under Johan Hendrik Caspar Kern and later served as Keeper at the National Museum of Indonesia (~1884–1905).

Jan Michał Rozwadowski was a linguist and Indologist who studied at Jagiellonian University and Leipzig under Karl Brugmann and August Leskien. He served at Jagiellonian University, becoming Professor and Head of the Department of Comparative Linguistics in 1904.

Jan Mrázek works in history, archaeology, and linguistics. He completed his doctoral studies under supervisor Josef Zubatý (-1925) and served as an Associate Professor at the National University of Singapore (attested 2011).

Jan N. Bremmer is a scholar of religious studies and history/archaeology. He completed PhD studies at Vrije Universiteit Amsterdam and the University of Amsterdam, subsequently holding academic posts at Utrecht University (1974–1990) and the University of Groningen (1990–2005).

Jan Nattier is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Sinology, and Central Asian studies. She earned her PhD at Harvard under Masatoshi Nagatomi, and held professorships at Indiana University Bloomington (1992–2005) and Soka University (2004–2010).

Jan Niecisław Baudouin de Courtenay was a linguist and Indologist who completed his Ph.D. at Leipzig (~1869–1870). He held professorships at Kazan, Tartu, Jagiellonian University, Saint Petersburg State University, and the University of Warsaw.
Jan P. Hogendijk is a historian and Indologist who earned his doctorate at Utrecht University (-1983). He has held professorships at Utrecht University (2005–2020) and Leiden University (2004–2009).

Jan Peter F. Hintelmann is a scholar in Buddhist studies who earned his PhD at the University of Hamburg under Marianne Pieper. He also studied under traditional teachers including Thupten Nyandak, Tenzin Kunga, Sonam Senge, and Geshe Sonam Rinchen.
